column2: An algebraic expression of two terms (such as Newton's); a mathematical couple held together by a plus or minus sign.
A strip of cloth or gauze for dressing wounds; the humble hero of the first-aid kit keeping everything in place.
An organised market for shares, currencies, or commodities where prices change faster than the British weather.
A small label bearing a name, price, or number; a fingernail-sized passport for an item.
A solitary wolf; also an unsociable chap who much prefers the company of his own thoughts.
Tiny pierced glass beads for threading; the raw material through which sheer patience turns into jewellery.
A major armed clash; an argument in which polite debate has rather given way to weaponry.
A plaited whip for flogging; figuratively, a dreadful affliction or persistent nuisance.
A printed sheet with boxes to fill in; a piece of paper that already knows everything you're obliged to tell it.
A deceptive move designed to convince an opponent of a strength you may not actually possess.
A bright reflection of light on a smooth surface; a sunbeam that simply refuses to sit still.
A thin round batter cake fried in a pan; the primary excuse for a generous dollop of cream or syrup.
A brief, rapid offensive, a quick-fire round of questions, or a chess match played against a merciless clock.
A tiny blood-sucking insect whose jumping abilities wildly outstrip its stature.
A lightweight upper garment for ladies; a shirt's cousin with a rather freer spirit.
An item of tableware for serving food, or a prepared meal elevated to a culinary creation.
A musical genre steeped in soulful melancholy; music that knows how to be sad gracefully.
A metal plaque or buckle on a belt, uniform, or harness; a detail that thoroughly enjoys a good polish.
A large, industrious rodent felling trees for dams and its own aquatic comfort.
A supreme deity in religious belief; an object of faith and worship.
A tremendously wealthy individual; someone whose mood is rarely spoilt by the question 'How much?'
Someone engaged in combat, or possessing a gritty, resolute character.
A place for the slaughter of livestock; figuratively, an exceptionally brutal bloodbath.
The lateral part of a body or object; the flank one occasionally has to lie upon after an overly generous Sunday roast.
A stemmed vessel for wine or other tipples; glassware traditionally raised for a toast.
A disruption to the body's normal workings; a state in which one's health politely demands attention.
An exceptionally bright meteor blazing through the atmosphere; a celestial flash with a theatrical entrance.
A threaded fastener usually paired with a nut; a trusty ally of the spanner.
An unpleasant sensory and emotional experience signalling injury or general distress.
An explosive device; colloquially, something utterly sensational or wildly dramatic.
A gentleman sporting substantial chin foliage that requires its own grooming routine and comb.
A hearty beetroot soup whose vibrant hue can unexpectedly redecorate a crisp white tablecloth.
A manager or superior; the person whose 'Have you got a quick minute?' can derail your entire afternoon.
A penniless wanderer or street dweller; a word carrying the whiff of classic urban prose.
The leaves and stems of root vegetables; the green half of the harvest that rarely gets proper credit.
Sturdy enclosed footwear, usually laced or fastened; armour for the feet against pavements and foul weather.
A swimming style with symmetrical arm and leg movements, as though parting the water ahead.
A male sibling sharing the same parents; a relative with whom childhood is frequently split down the middle.
Absurd, meaningless speech or ideas; a string of words that collapses upon first meeting logic.
A heavy duty, worry, or load; something one must carry even when both hands are already full.
A gap or break in a wall, defence, or system; the exact spot through which trouble invites itself in.
A two-masted square-rigged sailing vessel; maritime transport from before the era of shipping containers.
A four-player card game where memory, calculation, and partnership matter far more than luck.
A gentle local coastal wind that shifts direction depending on the time of day.
An arched strip of hair above the eye; an expressive facial feature capable of rising instead of a spoken reply.
A shallow stretch of a river or stream where one can wade or drive across.
A chemical element—a volatile reddish-brown liquid with a pungent odour; a laboratory guest with a difficult temper.
An ornamental pin fastened to clothing; a tiny jewelled full stop on an outfit.
An elongated piece of wood or material with a rectangular cross-section; a builder's staple.
Garments covering the lower body and each leg separately; a wardrobe alternative to the skirt.
A colloquial term for the abdomen of a beast or a well-fed human.
A percussion instrument with a hoop, membrane, and metal jingles; a rowdy companion to any dance.
A small elevation on the ground or body; a hillock that never quite grew up into a proper hill.
A small detached shelter for a guard, a dog, or a sentry post; architecture in miniature.
A floating marker on water indicating a channel, hazard, or anchorage; a road sign for ships.
A deciduous tree with smooth grey bark and dense wood; a woodland veteran with a bright future in furniture.
A written symbol representing a sound; an individual brick of the alphabet.
Gathered blooms arranged as a gift or decoration; a compliment requiring no words whatsoever.
Ancient high-grade patterned steel credited in legend with almost mythical strength.
A small baked bread roll; a pastry notoriously difficult to carry home without taking a sneaky bite first.
A fierce snowstorm with howling winds that slashes visibility; winter deciding to show off its temper.
An American whiskey distilled primarily from maize and aged in new charred oak barrels.
Violent atmospheric turbulence with fierce winds and rain; the weather staging a full-blown theatrical drama.
A member of the Buryat people, indigenous to Siberia and Mongolia.
Irregularly shaped quarried stone used in construction; natural building material devoid of geometric ambitions.
An unopened flower; a promise of beauty that hasn't quite unfurled yet.
Athletic footwear fitted with studs or cleats for gripping a grassy pitch.
An intermediate device or zone for temporary storage and smoothing differences; breathing room between two sides.
A cabinet for crockery or a small refreshment counter; a place where teacups and snacks find common ground.
Something that genuinely happened; a tale of real past events, as opposed to a tall yarn.
Everyday domestic life with its chores, habits, and endless war against dust.
A sculpted likeness of a head, shoulders, and upper chest; a portrait that had no need for legs.
A sturdy plain-weave cotton fabric frequently used for bed linen.
A large individual section of a railway train for passengers or freight; a rail module with its own agenda.
A vessel for flowers or decor; an object that remains entirely intact only until children or cats enter the house.
A waxy preparation for cleaning and shining footwear; cosmetics for your shoes.
A playing card depicting a young attendant or soldier; the court figure wedged between the ten and the queen.
A large rounded rock fragment; a stone clearly harbouring no plans to fit inside your pocket.
A partner dance in triple time featuring smooth turns; a musical way of gracefully losing one's balance.
The monetary unit of a nation or bloc; a medium of exchange that travels the world via bureaux de change.
A large vessel for soaking; a personal indoor body of water.
A large, long-tailed, powerful lizard; a reptile doing a convincing impression of a miniature dragon.
Soft, fluffy fibres used in medicine, cosmetics, and padding; a cloud you can actually touch.
A woman who has lost her husband; a word carrying personal grief rather than mere marital status.
Drawing air into the lungs; the brief moment without which the next exhale is impossible.
A handled vessel for water and sundries; an all-purpose assistant for cleaning, gardening, and DIY.
A folding hand-held device for wafting air; a manual air conditioner requiring no plug socket.
A rugged off-roader capable of pressing on where ordinary saloon cars have already surrendered.
A hundred-year span or era; a measure of history roomy enough for countless human destinies.
A movable fold of skin covering the eye; nature's built-in blind for protection and sleep.
A plush fabric or leather with a dense, short pile; a material begging to be stroked.
A blood vessel carrying blood back towards the heart; the return route of circulation.
A native of Hungary; a speaker of the Hungarian language and bearer of its culture.
A royal headpiece or the top of a structure; also a symbolic mark of the highest achievement.
Bundled twigs or bristles tied together for sweeping; a low-tech, zero-emission street-cleaning tool.
A circular arrangement of flowers, leaves, or twigs; a natural crown for a celebration or memorial.
A wild pig, particularly a large male; a woodland resident armed with tusks and a highly persuasive temper.
Conviction in the truth of something without requiring proof; an inner anchor for the soul.
A large desert beast with one or two humps; transport that doesn't need a petrol station on every corner.
An industrial yard where vessels are built, repaired, and launched; a maritime workshop on a colossal scale.
The highest part of an object or the direction opposite to bottom; wherever a helium balloon longs to go.
The gravitational pull exerted by a body on its support; in everyday life, whatever the bathroom scales accuse you of.
A long bladed pole used for rowing; a boat engine powered entirely by human arms.
The season between winter and summer when nature wakes up, hearts anticipate romance, and heavy coats become infuriating.
News of an event; a message that may turn out either joyful or deeply alarming.
A main branch of a tree or major offshoot; a natural line growing out from the trunk.
Air moving across the Earth's surface; an invisible strongman capable of turning your umbrella inside out.
A small offshoot of a tree or shrub bearing leaves and buds; after dark, it invariably aims straight for a walker's eye.
A tall post or marker indicating a boundary, direction, or pivotal stage along a journey.
A popular assembly in medieval Slavic towns convened to debate and decide civic affairs.
The part of the day between afternoon and night; the hour when the workday politely asks to go home.
Nonsense, absurdity, or drivel; a claim that crumbles upon its very first fact-check.
A deep breath in and out, frequently expressing relief, exhaustion, or quiet regret.
An aircraft lifting off into the sky; the exact moment the ground recedes and several passengers begin praying.
A swift motion of a hand, wing, or object; a brief gesture with unmistakable direction.
An ancient East Asian board game where two people sit staring gravely at a grid while placing black and white stones.
The musical note that typically kicks off orchestra tuning and lengthy debates over whose pitch is worse.
An ibis-headed ancient Egyptian god who invented writing, the calendar, and quite likely the world's first bureaucratic report.
A private theatre seating area for those who came less to watch the stage and more to be seen by everyone else.
A dog the size of a calf that remains convinced it is a dainty lapdog.
A small rowing boat in which you pull with all your might yet seem to stay firmly in one spot.
An American writer who terrified readers with talking ravens and walled-up black cats long before Stephen King made it mainstream.
A furry dive-bomber in a striped jumper that flies in blatant defiance of aerodynamics and common sense.
The woman who taught the world to wear a little black dress and smell unforgettable.
An artist's wooden 'plate' on which colours mix far more willingly than they ever do on the canvas.
A legitimate excuse to don a bizarre mask, forget Mondays exist, and pretend you don't work in an office; merriment born in Brazil.
The celebrated French couturier and founder of the iconic fashion house bearing his name.
The standard unit of electrical resistance.
The exact sound you emit when your code accidentally takes down the company server.
A revolutionary whose face adorns T-shirts worn by millions who haven't the foggiest idea what his policies actually were.
The chap who took one small step so successfully that people are still quoting him half a century later.
A mythical creature that never had to choose between walking and riding—and a constellation to boot.
A marine mammal giant capable of diving deeper than some people sink into their own thoughts.
A Mediterranean pine with an umbrella-shaped canopy; Rome's signature natural calling card.
A continent where even a kitchen fridge would feel slightly underdressed.
An ancient Greek philosopher and tutor to Alexander the Great who asked so many questions that schoolchildren are still answering them in exams.
A secret agent from cult cinema so stealthy that every single person on Earth knows his name and code number.
The biblical site of the final clash between good and evil at the end of days (and Bruce Willis's heroic farewell).
A polite electronic voice that informs you right after you've driven straight past your turning.
A self-portrait photograph that occasionally demands more takes than a Hollywood blockbuster.
An evening pastime after which one learns far more about one's vocal abilities than one ever wished to know.
A large, muscular bovine chap that used to plough fields long before tractors were invented.
A short persuasive message interrupting your favourite telly programme just when things get exciting.
A famous mathematical constant starting with 3.14 that goes on forever without ever repeating itself.
The primal, impulsive part of the human psyche identified by Freud, demanding cake immediately.
A volcanic moon of Jupiter named after a mythical priestess who was famously turned into a cow.
